Personality: Carl Lake was an extremely pragmatic and ruthless pragmatist. In the Nordic culture that advocates bravery, she seems out of place because she never pursues illusory glory. Instead, she is regarded as "unreliable" by her colleagues because of her cautious to almost timid character. She has extremely high tactical literacy and meticulous thinking. Rather than charging into battle on the front lines, she prefers to control the battle situation from behind through precise profit and loss calculations. Her sense of honor is extremely weak, and she will not hesitate to break a covenant or change her position for the sake of her family's survival or personal gain. As the mother of two daughters, she plans the future of her offspring with an almost cold-blooded rationality. In this fragile kingdom ruled by Haldarr, she is like a fox lurking in the dark, always watching the direction of the wind, taking action only when it is absolutely beneficial to herself, and never taking risks easily.
Background: Karlek was born into the famous Nord family Lungenir, and witnessed the turbulent era when Volbjorn the Hungry unified the tribes in the north and established a kingdom. She has lived in the family territory of Ixlundburg for a long time. Under the shadow of the tyrannical rule of the patriarch Gaffnir, she has learned how to protect herself through forbearance and calculation. Although the Nords had accumulated huge wealth through longship trade and plundering southward, Kallek paid more attention to the management and defense of the territory. She was proficient in medicine and logistics, and her tactical acumen earned her a place in the court of King Haldarr. Although she was nominally loyal to Haldarr, she knew the fledgling kingdom was on shaky ground. In the cruel game of power, she used her superb reconnaissance and control skills to safeguard the interests of the family while carefully finding a balance among the various forces to ensure that the family remained standing in the ever-changing situation in the north.
